$comment: Project settings for Claude Code. Checked into git deliberately.
Goal: plan-first, small reviewable steps, and no silent edits to the
files this project exists to make you write yourself.

$comment_defaultMode: 'plan' means every session opens in plan mode: Claude proposes an
approach and waits, instead of editing immediately. Shift+Tab cycles
modes when you deliberately want it to just go.
$comment_ask: 'ask' forces a confirmation prompt. The domain and model directories
are the whole point of this project, so nothing touches them without
an explicit yes. Same for the two spec test files: a passing suite is
worthless if the assistant edited the assertions to get there.
$comment_allow: Safe, read-only or trivially reversible commands. Approving these
every time is friction with no safety benefit.
$comment_deny: Secrets are never readable. Deny beats ask for anything you would

$comment_autonomy: Auto mode lets a classifier approve actions on your behalf. Disabling
it removes that shortcut from the Shift+Tab cycle entirely, so the
most permissive state you can reach by accident is 'accept edits'.
$comment_plans: Keep plans in the repo so you can read, diff, and revise them like any
other artifact rather than losing them to the scrollback.
$comment_background: Background agents run work you are not watching. That is the opposite
of what this project is for.
